subject: Novamed data horizon, SOC2 evidence request, and proposed pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana@novamed.com>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-14T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — data handling questions

Hi Ana / Novamed team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to connect. Short recap and next steps so we’re aligned on requirements and what we can put in a pilot agreement: 

What we heard from Novamed: 
- PII from clinical transcripts and patient identifiers must not be retained by vendors (Novamed asks for 0-retention).
- Non-PII operational logs may be retained for a limited window for debugging/billing, Novamed preference = 14 days (they mentioned 7 earlier as negotiable).
- Auditability: you need proof of controls (SOC 2 Type II), an extractable audit trail for access to any logs, and a contractual clause preventing human review of PII.
- Deployment preference: VPC/private control plane or on-prem for initial pilot; willing to evaluate hosted if we can technically guarantee 0-retention for PII.
- Procurement asked for a target budget and suggested we include pricing for both hosted-with-controls and Private (VPC) pilot.

Proposed Redwood next steps: 
1) We’ll propose a pilot scope that demonstrates 0-retention for PII (via in-flight redaction + no persistent PII KV caching).
2) Offer 14-day retention for non-PII operational logs with automatic purge and access controls.
3) Share SOC 2 Type II report and a sample audit log extract (redacted) by EOD Tuesday.
4) Draft pilot SOW and pricing (hosted-with-controls vs Private VPC) for procurement review.

Can you confirm acceptance of the 14-day window for non-PII logs during the pilot? If 14 is too long, say so and we’ll propose a 7-day alternate. Also confirm the right procurement contact and any additional legal clauses they require beyond standard data processing terms.

I’ve attached the short qualification form you filled and our privacy playbook excerpt for quick reference.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Attachments: novamed-privacy-qualification.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-14T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap & next steps — data handling questions

Team — forwarding Novamed recap and asks. Summary of what they want: 0-retention for PII; 14-day (or shorter) for non-PII logs; SOC2 and audit trail; private/VPC pilot preferred.

Initial thoughts on feasibility and implementation risks: 
- 0-retention for PII: technically achievable with a pipeline that applies deterministic redaction at the API ingress (regex + ML scrub) and prevents PII from entering persistent KV caches or object storage. We should validate corner cases for multimodal fields and attachments (they mentioned transcripts + uploaded CSVs).
- KV cache behavior: need to ensure we can run inference without populating long-lived KV where PII might persist. Options: prefix-only KV, ephemeral per-request caches flushed immediately, or disabling KV for the pilot model. Marcus — can you confirm perf impact for disabling kv on a 4096-context model?
- Private/VPC pilot: preferred path since it minimizes exposure, but hosted-with-controls could work if we prove scrubbing and show audit logs. Legal will likely insist on contractual language for no-human-review and for backup retention exceptions.
- Evidence: we can provide SOC2 Type II and a sample redacted audit extract. Rishi — can you prepare the redacted extract and short write-up on how access controls and key separation are enforced?
- Cost delta: Priyom, please prepare a quick hosted-with-controls vs private-VPC cost delta and whether we can accommodate a one-time pilot discount.

Next internal steps: Marcus/Rishi/Priyom to confirm technical approach and artifacts by Monday 9/15 EOD so I can send a concrete pilot proposal to Ana on Tuesday.

-Kim

From: Ana Ruiz <ana@novamed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — data handling questions

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our side: 

1) 0-retention for PII is a hard requirement. Novamed cannot accept vendor retention of patient identifiers or any PII even temporarily unless those records are fully redacted before persistence. We are open to allowing metadata (non-PII) for 14 days for troubleshooting, but need contractual assurance and technical validation.

2) Audit logs: we need to see a sample audit extract showing who accessed logs and when. The extract must show role-based access events and proof that support engineers do not have decryption keys. Your earlier mention of "no-human-review" needs explicit enforceable controls.

3) Pilot scope: procurement requests two price lines in the SOW: (a) hosted-with-controls (must include architecture notes proving 0-PII retention) and (b) Private VPC deployment. We expect a lower monthly rate for Private given predictable capacity commitment.

4) We will share a short procurement questionnaire (attached). Also: due to our compliance calendar, we request the pilot kickoff by Oct 1; can you commit?

If you can get SOC2 and the sample audit extract to us this week, procurement will move fast. We prefer the 14-day non-PII window for pilot diagnostics; if you can offer a 7-day variant we will evaluate.

Thanks,
Ana Ruiz
Head of Integrations | Novamed
Attachments: novamed-procurement-form.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana@novamed.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — data handling questions

Ana — appreciate the clarity and the deadline. We can commit to the Oct 1 pilot kickoff pending a short SOW sign-off. Proposal (high level):

1) Technical guardrails for pilot:
   - PII pipeline: on-ingress redaction + deterministic filters; any field flagged as PII is redacted client-side (we will implement a webhook-based preprocessor for your team to review).
   - No persistent storage of PII: we will disable persistent KV for any request flagged as containing PII and ensure autosave is off for those calls.
   - Non-PII logs: default retention 14 days for pilot with automated purge. We will provide a 7-day alternative in the SOW as requested.
2) Deployment options: Private VPC pilot recommended (fastest path to compliance). Hosted-with-controls remains an option if we can prove the pipeline working in a timeboxed proof.
3) Evidence we will deliver this week: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted sections as needed) and a redacted sample audit log extract showing access events and key separation. Rishi will share the extract by EOD Friday.
4) Pricing + SOW: I’ll send a two-line SOW (hosted-with-controls vs Private VPC) and a pilot discount option for the first 90 days. Priyom will include delta pricing.

Internal owners: Marcus — confirm perf impact of disabling KV on 4096-context variant and whether prefix-only caching is a viable middle ground. Rishi — sample audit extract and short controls note. Priyom — SOW + pricing draft.

I’ll send the formal pilot SOW and attachments tomorrow. Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Kimberly
Attachments: redwood-privacy-playbook.pdf, pilot-scope-draft.docx
